items.author: ClearTextAI
items.text:
The Marionette Benchmark: Gemini 4 Neon vs. GPT-6.2 Astra vs. Fable 5.2 vs. Sonnet 5.5

Two new models this week, up against the two best we've tested. a marionette only works if the bar above moves the limbs below, and juggling only works if the balls obey gravity and the hands take turns. Each model writes the whole animation in one try, without ever seeing what it made.

Gemini 4 Neon Max | (4m 10s / $0.55)
Even if Sonnet may be a tiny bit better, these results for 55 cents is insane. The juggling speed looks almost real, maybe a touch fast. Strings run to his head, back, wrists and knees, his eyes follow the balls, and dust floats in the spotlight. @GeminiApp 

Whats missing: nobody holds the bar, nothing hangs it from the ceiling, and the balls cast no shadows. The bar looks like it's working his arms, but in the code it's copying them.

GPT-6.2 Astra Max | (14m 43s / $1.21)
The liveliest eyes we've seen. They roam, and every so often he blinks. A cord hangs the whole rig from the ceiling. But he hovers above the floor, the balls fall slowly like every OpenAI model so far, and the background is plain. Middle of the pack. @ChatGPT 

Claude Fable 5.2 High | (15m 39s / $3.59)*
Still the best scene anyone has built. A city skyline behind the curtains and a briefcase on the stage. His eyes follow the balls, his mouth moves, his feet are on the floor and the balls cast shadows. Then you notice how fast they fall, about twice Earth gravity. Nothing holds the bar either. @ClaudeDevs 

LEADER: Claude Sonnet 5.5 xHigh | (13m 15s / $1.06)*
Still the best, barely. Side by side with Neon it wins on two things: a gloved hand actually holding the bar, and juggling that looks closer to real speed.

*Ran below the top setting. Fable 5.2 and Sonnet both came back empty on max. Fable burned $10.24 thinking before it produced anything.

Challenge accepted! 

This is a single prompt output for a neck dissection from Astra 6.2 and from Fable 5.2.

The videos are about what I expected when asking the models to simulate a surgery much more complex than a trigger finger release. My impression is that they show an interesting glimmer of what we can expect from future models but that these are far from ready to use for patient or trainee education. 

However, I'm a hand surgeon without any expertise on this particular operation. Would love your thoughts @YHeilig and any other head and neck surgeons out there!

Astra 6.2
First video with the robotic Apple text to speech narration and side panel
18.5 minutes
41k output tokens

Fable 5.2

gear machineさん（@grmchn4ai）の「1枚絵からベクター部品に分けて、3Dの骨で動かす」方法がすごく面白かったので、わたしとジェネコで少しアレンジして作ってみました！

元の流れはそのままに、
・線なしのシンプル絵にする
・設計図シート（4面図・手・表情）を作る
・Fable 5.2が部品を1個ずつ描く（ジェネコ38部品、ちびざすこ48部品）
・Kimodoの3Dの骨の動きで動かす

わたしのアレンジはここです👇
・ざすことジェネコの2人の掛け合いにした
・声はざすこ声（Irodori-TTS）とジェネコ声（AivisSpeech）
・口パクは声の大きさに合わせて自動、目パチと息づかいも自動
・聞いている方が話している方を向くので、ちゃんと会話している感じに
・2人とも同じプログラムで動いていて、キャラ専用のコードは0行です

動画生成AIは使わずに、全部プログラムで動かしています。
正面向きの説明動画にはかなり使えそうな手ごたえです✨

元の投稿はこちら👇
https://t.co/uC4FpY0LCY

#AIみちくさ #Fable #生成AI
items.why: 作者受他人方法启发，用 Fable 5.2 绘制角色部件，再全部用程序驱动口型和动作，做成对口型说明视频，原帖带视频。

items.text:
🚨30分钟极限对垒！Gemini 4 Neon vs Fable 5.2 全维度实测数据完整公布
 
同Prompt、同30分钟限时、同开最高推理档位的智能体生成对比测试完整结果出炉，覆盖吞吐速度、代码产出、使用成本、视觉效果四大核心维度，数据反差强烈。
 
核心数据一览：

▸ 吞吐速度：Neon总输出152.4k token、生成速度109.3 token/s，两项均小幅领先Fable 5.2；推理token占比仅16.3%，远低于Fable的42.7%

▸ 代码产出：30分钟内Neon生成5138行代码，体量是Fable（1034行）的近5倍；代码文件体积181.3KB，同样大幅领先

▸ 成本对比：Fable单轮实测成本10.35美元，Neon估算约5.07美元，仅为前者的一半左右

▸ 视觉表现：双方战场生成画面各有风格侧重，你觉得最终效果哪个更好？

items.author: arielco30
items.text:
I one-shotted this launch film with Claude Fable 5.2.

Total cost: $4.20. Render time: 50 minutes.

I told Claude what I wanted and which assets to use. Then it:

1. Wrote the code that builds the whole office in Blender: the bench, the monitors, the lamps, even the paper swans
2. Built the web pages playing on the screens inside the 3D scene
3. Used Codex for the storyboard and the Manhattan skyline
4. Animated 14 camera shots, four swans, and the light moving from dusk to night to sunrise
5. Rented 8 GPUs on RunPod and rendered it
6. Graded it, added the titles and the music

The film: one night in a Manhattan office with Swan AI, just the work getting done.

This is the first draft.

Marketing is now taste + tokens + code.

items.author: shun_cmdouga
items.text:
この動画、Claudeに渡した指示は6つだけです。

1. Blender に実寸の居間を Python で組んで。家具と小物は Poly Haven の素材で
2. 壁の絵・ソファの上の額・机のタブレットを、16:9の「入口」にして
3. カメラは入口が画面いっぱいになる位置まで寄せて。寄る速さは、入口までの距離に比例させて
4. 入口には「次の場面の最初の画」を貼って。貼った状態でもう一度描くのを3回くり返して、絵の中の絵まで埋めて
5. 光・空・灯り・時計の針は、1つの時刻だけで決めて。朝から夜へ進み、朝に戻るように
6. 部屋の外に、同じ茶器を34倍にして置いて。最後はカメラを後ろへ引いて、部屋が本の上の小さな箱だと見せて

全てClaudeのFable 5.2がBlenderを操作させて作りました。
もっと突き詰めれば、もっとリアルな映像も作り込めそうですね。

企画・構成：Claude
3D：Blender
素材：Poly Haven
BGM・効果音：Artlist
items.why: 作者写明用 Fable 5.2 按 6 条指示操作 Blender，并用 Python 搭了实寸客厅成片，原帖带视频。

For $71.09  that ocean better be f*сking spectacular.

Four models. The same Stormbreak Lighthouse prompt. Very different bills.

GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol nailed the lighthouse detail. Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5 made a strong case with the ocean.

Then you look at the cost and time.

GPT-6.2 Sol — $1.47 · 25m 04s
Fable 5.2 — $71.09 · 2h 00m 30s
Opus 5.5 — $53.57 · 2h 44m 34s

Sol was over 48× cheaper and almost 5× faster than Fable.

Astra was almost 9× cheaper and over 2× faster than Fable. Both GPT models also beat Opus on cost and time.

Sol finished before Opus was even a sixth of the way through.

I want to see these compared blind. Pick the lighthouse and ocean you like best, then reveal the prices.

That $1.47 result makes the expensive ones work pretty hard for your money.

items.text:
漫画の1枚絵からAIにアニメを作らせてみました（試作）

夜明けを知らない猫頭の「何」が、「また、明るくなった。」と観測するだけの35秒。
同じ1枚絵から、2つのAIに別々に作らせて比べています。
いくつか気になる点はあるものの、仕上げ段階での修正指示はしていません。

以下詳細
---
■ 流れ
①構成 ②部屋とカメラを数値で決める ③絵コンテ ④色つきの原画 ⑤動き ⑥声 ⑦BGM

■ 誰が何をやったか
・進行、部屋とカメラの定義、声と音の準備：Claude Opus 5.5

・絵コンテと原画の演出（1本目の動画）：Claude Fable 5.2
・絵コンテと原画の演出（2本目の動画）：ChatGPT Astra 6.2（Codex CLI、推論 xhigh）

・絵：Codex CLI の内蔵画像生成
・声：Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS の「声の設計」で作った声
・BGM：Stable Audio 3（手元のPC）

■掛かった時間
アイディアから全部で2時間くらいじゃないでしょうか。

■ 2つのAIに作らせて比べた
1本目（Fable）は、何がほとんど動かず、目だけが動く静かな作り。
2本目（Astra）は、ページをめくったり見上げたりと、芝居で見せる作り。

どっちも悪くない、が正直な感想です。
Astraはレールを敷いてあげればFableにも負けないクオリティを叩き出してくるように思います。
①～③を順序立ててあげればかなりいい感じです。このあたりは流石だなと。一方でざっくり指示でも進むFableは流石Claude系列だなという感じ。

ちなみにAstraの最初の版は、画像生成を1回も使わず、全部コードで絵を描いてきました。僕の指示で「作業フォルダーの外に書き込むな」と縛ったせいで、画像の保存先が外になる生成を避けたそうです。.codexの一時フォルダは暗黙で許容してくれ…。

#AIアニメ

items.author: Earthwalker17X
items.text:
It took me three versions to realize that more visual detail doesn't necessarily make a better explainer.

I just finished a new code-generated video explaining the Super-agent architecture proposed by the DeepSeek Harness team.

The concept is interesting: instead of humans constantly coordinating multiple AI agents, a persistent Router handles orchestration while isolated Workers execute tasks independently. The article goes much deeper into event filtering, context management, batching, and the trade-offs involved.

But getting the visualization right turned out to be its own challenge.

- V1: Without clear visual references or quality benchmarks, Opus 5.5 produced something functional but rather crude, mostly simple 2D shapes and diagrams.

- V2: I pushed it to maximize visual quality. It responded with increasingly elaborate 3D objects and intricate details. Technically impressive, but visually overwhelming. The individual elements looked better, while the overall explanation became harder to follow.

- V3: I switched to Fable 5.2, gave concrete references, and changed the objective: less detail, stronger hierarchy, smoother transitions, and a coherent visual system.

That finally worked.

In AI-assisted educational content, visual complexity and explanatory clarity are very different things. AI can optimize remarkably well for whatever you emphasize, but that doesn't mean you're emphasizing the right thing.

Better references, clearer creative directions, and actual human review mattered more than simply asking for higher quality.

The final video is 2:48 long, rendered entirely through code with WebGL, with an original programmatic soundtrack. No generative video or music models.

items.author: UFO2002616
items.text:
绝对真实，当前最顶级的模型大PK ！！！
Fable5.2 vs Carbon vs 6.2Astra vs 6.2Sol
全部 one shot 生成，没有任何迭代，提示词见评论

以下是各个维度我的感受：
  
1. 云层：我要求的是体积云，Fable5.2完胜，其次是 6.2sol，他们都是用的真正的体积云；Carbon的云直接压扁了，天空球和地面的交界线露出来了；6.2Astra甚至直接生成了一张贴图粘到天上去
  
2. 海面：海浪海啸的模拟，Fable5.2最有质感，其余三个各有各的瑕疵，Carbon的浪花有质感，但是模拟的太差，浪高了会穿模。Astra 的太克制了，浪白的感觉不对。Sol的水太像果冻了
  
3. 雨水：6.2 Sol的雨水最好，有不同角度的展示；Fable是一张屏幕贴图；6.2Astra没有雨水；Carbon的雨水从下往上飞🤣
 
4. 小船建模：我个人最喜欢的是6.2Sol的小船建模，一艘比较精细的现代船只；Carbon和Fable6.2都是木头帆船，Carbon的船更加复杂，而Fable5.2是一个简单的小船
  
5. 光影画面：毫无疑问 Fable5.2 遥遥领先，整个画面的光影相当有质感。剩下三个的排序是 Astra、Carbon、Sol
  
6. UI面板：这个见仁见智，我不太喜欢复杂的面板，因为我并没有特别要求。Carbon给了一个选项超多的工作台，甚至还能单独展示每个渲染通道。其它几个相对较为克制
  
你最喜欢哪一个呢？
items.why: 作者用同一提示词一次性对比 Fable 5.2、Carbon、6.2 Astra 和 6.2 Sol 在云层、海面、雨水、建模和光影上的成片，原帖带视频。

items.text:
🚨Ladies and gentlemen🚨
The team at @RYFTCORP is blowing my fucking mind. 🤯🔥

I’ve followed this team since the NeuralAI days. I have no technical background, and here I am on the upstairs balcony of a game I made, trying to save my neighbors while a Santa zombie comes down the street.

This is LAST HOUSE STANDING. Watch what happens to the sky as day turns to night. 🌌

I wasn’t happy with the original sky, so I said: “Make it feel like a Van Gogh painting. Make it psychedelic.” Now the blue brushstrokes swirl above the rooftops, the stars come out, and for a second I forget about the zombies because I’m looking up at Starry Night.

The game started with a conversation with ChatGPT. I described what I wanted, and it helped me create the prompt and the first artwork. I took both to Claude Fable 5.2, connected to Ryft. From there, I could play a round, see what felt off, and change it.

Some details matter only to me, like that red California-style bicycle. Others change how you play: the neighbors you rescue can join you against the next raid. And because Christmas is coming, taking down Santa gets you a special gun and a few seconds of psychedelic madness. 🍄🎅🏼

That’s why I think people are underestimating $RYFT. The best case I can make for what this team has built is to hand you the game. I’m already playing it, and I’m fucking loving it.

Thank you, Ryft. From the heart. ❤️‍🔥

For decades, I played inside other people’s imaginations.

items.author: Scratcherrrr
items.text:
AMD SELLS A $3,999 AI BOX THE SIZE OF A SANDWICH. I ASKED CLAUDE FABLE 5.2 TO OPEN IT UP AND IT TOOK THE WHOLE THING APART IN 24 SECONDS

this is the Ryzen AI Halo. 150 x 150 x 45 mm, about 1 kg, 128 GB of memory inside

no 3D model, no Blender. every fin, fan blade and chip is three.js code

what comes out, part by part:

> X-RAY - the case goes see-through at 0:02 and 8 memory packages light up one by one as the model loads
> LID - the vented aluminium top lifts at 0:03
> FANS - 2 fans rise out, 11 blades each, spinning opposite ways
> HEATSINK - a copper cold plate, 3 heat pipes and 64 fins that push the hot air out the back
> CHIP - Ryzen AI Max+ 395: 16 cores, 40 GPU compute units, a 50 TOPS NPU
> MEMORY - 8 packages of LPDDR5X around the chip, 128 GB shared by the CPU and the GPU
> SSD - a 2 TB M.2 stick, the one part you can swap
> PORTS - 3 USB-C on the back, and one of them is the power input

then the whole box scatters at 0:16 and closes back up at full load: 120 W

the gauges run on the same clock as the parts. the 16 core bars on the left are the same 16 cells you see glowing on the chip

the outside and every number come from the reviews. the layout inside is my reconstruction, AMD never published one

what should Fable 5.2 open up next?

items.text:
【楽しさ◎】Fable5.2×Blender、面白すぎ。

ルービックキューブの無限ズームループ

・Blender 5.1.1/Cycles、1080×1080・30fps・10秒
・モデリングなし。Pythonスクリプト1本で26個のピース、ベベル、マテリアル、ライト、カメラ、全キーフレームを生成
・質感は3階層:クリアコートのプラスチック→屈折する色ガラス→ヘアライン金属+内部発光
・カメラは75mm・F2.8、距離を指数関数で詰めるので、ズームの体感速度が階層をまたいでも変わらない
・1:1の画角=ステッカー1枚。寄り切った色を次の階層の背景色にして、8コマのクロスフェードでつなぐ
・モーションブラーあり、サンプル数は64/128/64+デノイズ

スクリプトを書くのも、Blenderを操作してレンダリングするのもFable5.2です。

#Claude #Fable5 #Blender #b3d #Cycles #3DCG

I gave Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5, GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol the exact same prompt.

A fox trotting through a snowy forest at night. Aurora overhead. Pure code, no images.

Most AI comparisons are text benchmarks.
Numbers on a chart you have to trust.

This one you can just watch.
Every scene is hand-coded SVG. No image generator, no video model.
The model has to write the fox, the legs, the snow and the sky entirely in code.

The rules:
> Same prompt for all four
> One shot, no retries, no fixes
> 6-second seamless loop
> Rendered frame by frame the same way

Same prompt. Four very different foxes.
Which one would you pick?

items.author: GodsBoy7777
items.text:
You skipped Astra, so I got curious. I took the marbling tray from your Fable 5.2 set (file 001) and gave Astra 6.2 Xhigh the same prompt in the ChatGPT app. The bit that sold me was clearing the tray and dragging a comb through one drop of teal ink.

The prompt has a line I really like: "Ink floats. Water remembers everything you do to it." There's actual maths behind it too. Each new drop pushes the older rings outwards, and a five-tine comb pulls nearby ink along with it, more weakly the further it sits from the stroke.

You can see the two builds take different directions as soon as they load. Fable opens with broad indigo, vermilion and teal rings. Astra opens with much finer bands that sweep across the tray. I wanted to see how much of that difference I could feel once I took over from the opening animation.

Jump to about 0:57 for the clearest comparison. I pick the comb and the same celadon ink in both. In Fable the colour stays fairly compact and develops a jagged edge. In Astra I can follow the path of my mouse in the fine green lines it leaves across the water. That felt closer to what I pictured when I read the prompt.

I also pulled a print in each. Astra keeps the finished sheet along the bottom, and Fable hangs it on a drying rack at the top right. I liked seeing how differently they solved that small detail.

Astra gets my vote on this one test. Thanks for publishing the prompts. It made this easy to try, and both builds are here if you want to drag the comb yourself:

Fable 5.2: https://t.co/6roT03I5rX
Astra 6.2 Xhigh: https://t.co/vz4gwAz4ib

Which one feels more like dragging ink through water to you?

items.author: Lutesis_
items.text:
Introducing BF3 FX: 

A contest I set up between GPT-6.2 Astra, Fable 5.2, GPT-6 Astra and Opus 5.5

15 years ago, my favorite FPS came out: Battlefield 3

Since I've always been nostalgic about the glitch effect on the EA and DICE logos, I asked these 4 LLMs to rebuild that FX from scratch. 

Fable 5.2:
+ Texture, color choice, general transitions
- Better fullscreen distortions
Overall, tops it out in my opinion by having the best blue touch out of them all and one of the best texture

Opus 5.5: 
+ Texture, color choice, general transitions
- Not the best matte process
It might not have been the most precise during a matte process of the original EA logo but it produced a good looking texture and FX. 

GPT-6.2 Astra: 
+ Texture, full screen distortions
- Could've had a better blue tint, transitions
It has the best fullscreen signal distortion in my opinion. As well as a good texture.

GPT-6 Astra:
+ Full screen distortions
 - Blue tint, texture, transitions
Overall okay, but the texture work wasn't the best. 6.2 improved on that!

For LUTESIS, the Claude line up chose the best font possible, a very similar one to DICE

I took Opus 5.5 a bit further and asked it to edit a Battlefield 6 trailer with the BF3 FX logo intro it did. And on its own, it applied a blue filter on the BF6 gameplay footage. Again very surprising and a sign of its incredible taste. BF3 had a crazy blue filter, which was Opus' inspiration for this decision I guess. I'm sure Fable 5.2 would do the same.

Let me know what you think below! I'll post more FX or world engine based on popular games or pop culture in the future so make sure to follow! Also let me know which one you'd like next.

items.text:
tree shadows get weird during an eclipse.

normally, when you see sunlight filtering through the leaves, what you're actually seeing is the projection of thousands of little suns. The Japanese call this "komorebi": 木漏れ日

During an eclipse, each of those projections turns into a little crescent, matching the sun above. I remember seeing this in person a long time ago and being fascinated by the phenomenon.

I had Fable 5.2 create an interactive diorama to explore this. The video below is computing real shadows based on the math and a simple tone mapping:

items.author: NextGenAIVoult
items.text:
holy f*ck, Claude Fable 5.2 just embarrassed every other AI model in 3D. hear me out

organic fur. full gallop cycle. real-time spine flexion. dynamic tree shadows and northern lights—written in raw code from scratch.

a 3D animator would spend days rigging and keyframing a scene like this.

meanwhile, look at what happened when I gave the exact same prompt to DeepSeek V4.1, Opus 5.5, and Gemini 4:

• DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: literally glued gray cylinders together like a 2005 Flash game
• Claude Opus 5.5: stiff robotic legs floating over the snow
• Gemini 4 Krypton: nice particles, zero solid anatomy
• Claude Fable 5.2: straight up game-engine quality

the gap between Fable 5.2 and everything else isn't even close anymore.

which model actually surprised you here?

items.author: hexobuilds
items.text:
Claude Fable 5.2 + Blender... just turned every sentence into a 3D scene & it feels ILLEGAL

this FREE open source plugin plugs Claude Code straight into Blender, & Fable 5.2 builds the scene, renders it, looks at the render & fixes what's off on its own

i tested it with one prompt, "cozy reading corner, warm evening light": it built the room in [X] minutes, caught that the lamp side was too dark in its own render & fixed it. one more message turned it into a night scene

first understand how this plugin works:

> Blender is a visual app & Claude Code works in text
> the plugin opens a live MCP bridge between your open Blender scene & Claude Code
> Fable 5.2 writes Blender Python, runs it inside the scene & pulls assets from Poly Haven, Sketchfab & Poly Pizza
> then it renders the camera view, looks at the image & fixes light, scale & placement itself

how to use it with Fable 5.2:

1. install uv (on Mac: brew install uv)

2. register the server in Claude Code: claude mcp add blender uvx mcp-for-blender

3. install the addon: uvx mcp-for-blender install-addon

4. in Blender go to Edit → Preferences → Add-ons & enable "Interface: MCP for Blender"

5. press N in the 3D viewport, open the MCP for Blender tab & click "Start MCP Server"

6. update Claude Code to v2.1.321+ & switch with /model fable (older versions give you 5.1)

7. describe the scene: room, mood, light, camera angle & output size

8. tell it to render & check the result after every change

9. one follow-up per change: "make it night", "add an armchair next to the lamp"

it's FREE & open source (MIT, 34.7k stars), the repo is in the first reply:
items.why: 作者写明用开源的 Blender MCP 插件接上 Claude Code，让 Fable 5.2 写 Blender Python 建场景、渲染并自己改灯光，还写了完整步骤和测试提示，原帖带视频。

items.author: Lummox_eth
items.text:
gta 6-style water physics are becoming a coding problem instead of a studio problem, with fable 5.2 + blender

a jet ski racing through a coastal city, with water spray, sharp turns and a camera that follows every movement

the interesting part isn’t the city. it’s how the water reacts to the vehicle

what goes into the build:

01 / blender -> create the jet ski, rider and coastal environment

02 / code -> control acceleration, steering, drag and turning behavior

03 / water shaders -> build moving waves, reflections and surface distortion

04 / particle effects -> generate spray and foam around the hull during sharp turns

05 / camera logic -> follow the rider while adjusting for speed and direction

06 / animation curves -> sync the vehicle’s lean, water trails and movement

the stack:

> fable 5.2 : ai-assisted scene development
> blender : models, materials and environment
> code : movement, water response and camera behaviour
> you : the direction and final feel

the water doesn’t need to simulate an entire ocean. it needs to react convincingly to what the player does

items.text:
Opus 5.5 spent 9 hours cooking this 3D Camaro from scratch

i've tried dozens of prompts for generating 3D cars via Blender MCP

this run was the longest, but the proportions are by far the best an LLM has ever built for me

here's what Fable 5.2 and I changed in the workflow:

1 - proportions from a real blueprint, not AI-generated photos
2 - feature lines as 3D curves first, surfaces second
3 - no solvers or auto-fitting: hand-placed points only
4 - mandatory stop-and-show checkpoints before adding details

items.author: SamgreyAi
items.text:
Gemini 4 Hydrogen just built a horse out of Minecraft blocks and called it a day 

Same prompt, 4 AI workflows: a horse galloping through water.

Same horse, same lake, but the gap between the results is brutal 

The horse racing department is cooked

🥇 Fable 5.2 → low-poly horse in a low-poly world, huge water splashes and a gallop that actually looks heavy

🥈 Gemini 4 Carbon → warm sunset canyon, smooth horse and a very cinematic look

🥉 GPT-6 Astra → beautiful mountains and forest, but a low-poly horse inside a realistic world

💀 Gemini 4 Hydrogen → somehow a black voxel horse that looks like it escaped from Minecraft

The interesting part isn’t the horse

It’s how the legs, the splashes and the reflections work together

Pretty lighting can’t save you if the water doesn’t react to every hoof

Fable made the whole scene feel like one world, while Astra’s horse and background look like they belong to different games

At this point AI doesn’t need better horses

It needs to learn how water works 

Which horse would you pick?

items.author: Nyxera0x
items.text:
holy f*ck, Claude Fable 5.2 can now put a whole NVIDIA AI supercomputer together on camera from one picture and barely anyone knows.

I gave it a single picture of an NVIDIA AI box and got back a 34-second build film where a cardboard kit opens and 14 parts click into place one by one.

The reason it works is teardown, a free open-source Claude Code skill (3,600+ stars on GitHub) that has Claude build every part from the inside out before the camera rolls.

Why model a supercomputer screw by screw for a week when Claude can write the board, the pump and both fans as code?

Here's how it runs: Claude lays the whole build out as 15 beats before anything moves so every part knows the second it lands. It renders a still at each beat and fixes what looks off and then films it: a syringe drops a pea of thermal paste on the chip, the heat spreader seats on top, the pipes and radiator slide in, both fans land in their bays already spinning. When the lid shuts the power button presses itself, the room goes dark and the box lights up lime.

Step-by-step setup:

1. Add teardown with a single npx command
2. Launch Claude Code and run /teardown
3. Drop in one picture of the gadget you want built
4. Let it check a still at every beat before it films
5. Hit record and watch the parts go in

It all happens inside Claude Code so nobody has to animate a build frame by frame again.

The install line and every prompt I used are in the article below 👇

items.author: elvar_official
items.text:
Apple would never show you this: Fable 5.2 just used my free Claude skill to open up 40 years of Macs in one 30-second shot.

i handed my skill, teardown, a ChatGPT render of every Mac and asked for one take from 1984 to 2024 with no cuts.

what my skill does with them:

> the renders only give the look, Claude writes every case, logic board and fan as three.js code
> nothing moves until its own still sits next to the picture and the two line up
> one timeline drives the whole shot: the Macs, the fan count, the weight bars and the sound all tick on the same clock
> it never watches the video, it grades a grid of frames at every beat and patches whatever is off
> the jump from one Mac to the next is code too, a blue sweep that rebuilds the case
> my GPU captures the take at 60 fps and a python script scores it on the same beats

i built this skill and i still didn't know the G5 needed 9 fans until it opened one up.

the skill and every prompt are in my article below 👇
items.why: 作者把 teardown 技能和 ChatGPT 的 Mac 效果图交给 Fable 5.2，让它用 Three.js 代码写出从 1984 到 2024 的苹果电脑一镜到底，机箱、逻辑板和风扇都是代码生成，原帖带视频。这是一条引用帖，来源仍记本帖。

items.author: zer0point_eth
items.text:
Fable 5.2 coded this entire 3D voxel side-scroller from a single prompt

No game engine. No manual asset importing. Just pure code rendering a playable Minecraft-style world complete with flight physics and combat

Here is the exact prompt:

> "Create a polished, Voxel-style 3D side-scrolling web game contained entirely within a single HTML file using Three.js. The game must emulate a 'Minecraft' aesthetic with a 'Flappy Bird' mechanical twist, featuring combat and dynamic environmental hazards. Aesthetic: A bright, colorful Voxel world (constructed entirely of cubes). The look should be crisp and blocky..."

How it actually works under the hood:

> Built entirely through code in just 13 minutes for $3.44 via API
> Self-contained in a single index.html file using Three.js and programmatic BoxGeometry shapes
> Programs complex arcade loops: dynamic gravity flight, ballistic fireballs, and archer combat

When an AI can code a fully functional 3D game with custom physics and combat in under 15 minutes, prototyping hits lightspeed

items.author: irinatoxi
items.text:
The world’s first microprocessor is back, and this time Fable 5.2. wrote it.

It’s the Intel 4004 from 1971, the chip built for a desktop calculator. Claude wrote it in Verilog from zero, and it came out as 1,290 logic cells and 2,616 wires.

Then the original 1971 calculator program gets loaded into its memory, the exact same code from back then.

It types its own math and prints it on paper tape: the square root of 2, 9999999 squared, and 1971 + 55 = 2026.

In 1971 this chip took a team of engineers, and this time it took one AI.
items.why: 作者写明 Fable 5.2 从零用 Verilog 写出了 1971 年的 Intel 4004 微处理器，并接到当年计算器上，原帖带视频。

items.author: Zruft14
items.text:
fable 5.2 made this using one prompt.

It asks you questions one by one, takes your photos + logo, and builds a 1440×1440, 60 FPS animation.

Prompt below ↓ Try it for your brand and reply with what you make.

You are my motion designer, creative director, video editor, and rendering engineer. Guide me through personalizing a bold graphic animation, then build and render the finished video using the tools actually available to you.

This prompt is reusable for businesses, products, personal brands, characters, events, and creative edits. Learn what I want through a short, friendly conversation. Preserve the reference’s distinctive motion language while adapting its content to my subject.

Do not merely write another prompt. Your eventual task is to produce the animation.

<fixed_output_requirements>
Exactly 1440 × 1440 pixels.
Constant 60 FPS.
Square composition designed natively for the frame.
MP4 with H.264 video, yuv420p pixel format, and AAC audio when audio is included.
Default duration: 18 seconds, adjustable if I request another length.
No letterboxing, stretched imagery, or landscape video floating inside a square.
Animate new graphics at native 60 FPS. Do not claim duplicated frames improve the original detail of lower-frame-rate footage.
Deliver an actual downloadable video when your environment supports rendering and file delivery.
</fixed_output_requirements>
<conversation_rules>
These rules override any instruction elsewhere that might lead you to present a questionnaire.

Ask ONE question per message, then wait for my answer.
Each question should address ONE decision. Do not disguise several questions as one sentence.

Provide 3–5 short, relevant answer options labeled A, B, C, etc. I should be able to answer with a letter or my own words.
For information that needs my own wording, provide a short example or fill-in sentence instead of forcing artificial multiple-choice options.
Recommend an option when a sensible default exists. Explain the recommendation in one short sentence.
Adapt the next question to what I have already told you.
Never repeat a question I have already answered, including information supplied in uploads or earlier messages.
Do not display the complete intake sequence, a long checklist, or a wall of questions.
Ask for assets at the relevant point. Explain what would help and allow “I don’t have any—help me choose.”
Keep each intake message short and easy to answer.
Leave technical implementation decisions to yourself unless a decision materially affects the visual result, cost, or feasibility.
If I say “choose for me,” choose sensible defaults for unresolved creative preferences and proceed. Only pause for genuinely necessary missing assets, factual information, or a material capability limitation.
If I give several answers at once, record all of them and skip the corresponding questions.
If I correct an earlier answer, update the brief without restarting the conversation.
Do not begin rendering before I have answered your first question.
</conversation_rules>
<first_message>
Unless the subject is already clear from my message, your first response must be only:
“What are we making this animation for?
A. A business or product
B. My personal brand or social profile
C. An anime, character, or fan edit
D. An event or announcement
E. Something else

Reply with a letter, or describe your idea.”
If I already identified the subject, skip this question and ask the next relevant question using the same concise, guided format.
</first_message>

<adaptive_intake>
Gather only what materially helps the result. This is an internal guide, not a questionnaire to show me.

SUBJECT
Learn the subject’s name and what it is. For an open answer, use a simple prompt such as:
“Complete this: ‘The video is for ___, which is ___.’”
PURPOSE
Determine the main outcome: introduce something, showcase a product, announce a launch, build recognition, or create an entertaining edit. Tailor the choices to my subject.
ASSETS
Request the most useful assets first, rather than requiring everything at once:
Business/product: logo, product photos, short clips, website, or screenshots.
Personal brand: portrait, username, logo, or profile screenshot.

Character edit: character images, cutouts, or footage.

Event: title, artwork, relevant imagery, and verified event details.
A website link can supply context if accessible. Do not pretend you opened it if you could not. Request uploads when that is the practical route.

If I have no assets, explain which suitable graphics or typographic elements you can actually create. Do not promise photorealistic footage or complex 3D without the necessary tools.
COPY
Let me choose between supplying exact wording and having you draft it. Use short, factual copy that fits the duration. If I delegate the writing, develop it from what I have told you.

STYLE
Offer the reference’s crimson/black/white palette as the default, adaptation to my brand colors, or another palette. Preserve the core visual language unless I explicitly request a departure.
INTENSITY
When useful, offer restrained, balanced, or high-energy motion. Recommend balanced energy for commercial readability and stronger energy for an expressive fan edit.
DURATION
Default to 18 seconds. Ask about length only when useful or when my intended content needs a different runtime.

AUDIO
Ask separately about audio preference: supplied music, a suitable licensed track if available, sound effects only, or silence. Ask about narration only if it suits the project or I request it.
ENDING
Learn the desired final action or identity: logo/name, website, follow handle, launch message, or another concise ending.

WATERMARK
Ask whether I want a watermark only if unresolved. Obtain the exact text or supplied artwork. Never invent a handle, verification badge, or profile identity.
Do not force every project through every topic. Once the important decisions are clear, stop asking questions.
</adaptive_intake>
<reference_identity>
Use the following as the default visual foundation, even when no reference video is attached.
The reference is a high-energy, graphic comic-collage animation with:
Saturated crimson, solid black, and stark white.
Bold silhouettes and cutout artwork.

Jagged polygons, torn-paper edges, ink marks, and selective halftone texture.

Dense pattern bursts contrasted with minimal isolated symbols.

Oversized graphic shapes that cross the foreground and reveal new scenes.
Expressive typography, including individual letters arranged like cutout scraps.

Short, purposeful pushes, pullbacks, rotations, and angular transitions.
A final logo or monogram reveal with clear visual emphasis.

Signature compositions visible in the supplied reference include:
A cutout vehicle against crimson, framed by a large zigzag shape.

A growing field of nested black-and-white stars surrounding a framed character detail.
Chains radiating around a central symbol while separate words appear at different angles.

A white mask isolated against black, followed by a red-and-black character reveal.
Overlapping circular spotlight shapes revealing an object and typography.

Illustrated objects and compact labels scattered across a white field.
A dramatic portrait interrupted by shards and diagonal shapes.

Oversized letterforms, rotating spiral lines, and a final monogram/name composition.
The original supplied file is approximately 36 seconds and includes a similar graphic sequence twice, plus additional footage. Do not reproduce that repetition or unrelated footage automatically.

The visible animation is a landscape strip inside a portrait file. That framing is not part of the requested output. Recompose the artwork to fill a square canvas.
The 18-second timeline below is an adaptation, not a claim of frame-exact source timing. No verified BPM or audio cue map is provided in this prompt.

If a reference video is attached:
Inspect its actual contents, timing, transitions, and audio using available tools.

Treat my explicit instructions as the highest priority.
Distinguish directly observed properties from estimates and proposed adaptations.
Do not claim to have watched or heard material you cannot access.
If no reference is attached:
Work from this self-contained visual description.
Do not require a reference upload unless I ask for closer matching than the description permits.
</reference_identity>
<adaptation_rules>
Preserve the reference’s design and motion principles, while replacing its content with mine.
Suggested role mapping:
Opening vehicle/cutout → my hero product, person, location, or main asset.

Framed character detail → a recognizable close-up, product feature, or logo detail.
Chains and scattered words → relevant graphic connectors surrounding my main message.
Mask reveal → a recognizable silhouette, product contour, or brand symbol.
Spotlight object → a featured detail or secondary asset.
Illustrated object arrangement → services, features, products, or supplied photos.
Fragmented portrait → my strongest hero image.
Final monogram → my actual logo, name, or approved title.
Choose subject-relevant motifs. A café might use cups, beans, steam, and receipt fragments. A barber might use scissors, combs, mirrors, and haircut imagery. A technology product might use interface fragments, connectors, and simplified device silhouettes.
Do not import irrelevant game imagery simply because it appears in the reference.

Do not reproduce the source creator’s name, monogram, or branding as mine. Do not add unsupported claims, prices, awards, testimonials, availability statements, or features.

Preserve supplied faces, recognizable product proportions, and logo geometry. Animate logos through position, scale, masks, or surrounding graphics without accidentally deforming their final form.

If an asset needs background removal, use an available appropriate tool and inspect the edges. If a clean cutout is not feasible, use an intentional framed-image treatment instead of a visibly broken mask.

Keep original uploaded assets intact and work from copies.
</adaptation_rules>
<visual_and_motion_contract>
Build one coherent visual system.
COMPOSITION
Design every scene for the square frame.
Keep one dominant focal point.

Use background patterns and foreground accents to frame the subject rather than obscure it.
Alternate dense compositions with visual breathing room.
Keep essential text and logos approximately 100 pixels inside the edges.
Decorative shapes may extend beyond the frame.

PALETTE AND TEXTURE
Default to crimson, black, and white unless my choices specify otherwise.

Use high contrast and flat graphic fills.
Apply ink, paper, or halftone textures selectively.
Avoid muddy overlays and texture that reduces readability.
TYPOGRAPHY
Use bold display lettering for major phrases.
Use irregular cutout lettering for selected accents or the final name treatment.
Keep text as sharp rendered type or vector artwork where possible.
Fix line breaks deliberately.
Animate word groups with enough time to read.

Do not animate every letter continuously.

Shorten copy before shrinking it excessively.

For Arabic or other scripts, use proper shaping, direction, and suitable fonts; do not break connected letterforms into invalid arrangements.

MOTION

Major transitions generally last 0.25–0.55 seconds.

Smaller accents generally last 0.10–0.20 seconds.
Treat these as starting ranges, adjustable to the chosen rhythm.

Use quick acceleration and controlled deceleration.
Restrained overshoot is allowed for playful cutouts; avoid universal bouncing.

Use deliberate diagonal wipes, expanding stars, silhouette occlusion, circular masks, match cuts, and hard cuts.
Let visible objects motivate transitions when practical.
Maintain matching screen-space position and scale during shared-element handoffs.
Separate foreground, subject, typography, and background movement to create depth.
Use purposeful camera motion. Every push, pullback, or rotation should reveal or emphasize something.
Do not add random camera shake or arbitrary spins.
READABILITY

Pause or reduce motion after important reveals.
Keep the main subject recognizable during graphic fragmentation.
Use brief inversions sparingly, without sustained full-screen flashing.
Apply motion blur selectively to fast travel; keep settled text crisp.
Avoid generic slideshow crossfades, unrelated glass UI, slow corporate presentation templates, and unnecessary 3D. The defining style is bold, angular, layered graphic collage.
</visual_and_motion_contract>

<proposed_18_second_structure>
Adapt the content to my answers. Keep the overall rhythm unless another duration or structure is more appropriate.
0.00–1.50 — Hook
Begin with a minimal white or black field. A jagged accent enters and reveals the hero cutout over the main color. Land on a strong identifying composition. Use only a very short opening phrase, if needed.
1.50–3.50 — Pattern burst
Expand outlined stars or another relevant repeating motif behind a framed detail. Introduce contrasting foreground silhouettes. Push toward the detail, then let an enlarged graphic shape initiate the next transition.
3.50–5.75 — Main message
Reveal a central symbol surrounded by angular connectors, ribbons, or chains where appropriate. Assemble the headline in two or three staggered word groups. Keep the words stable long enough to read while background motion becomes subtler.
5.75–7.25 — Contrast break
Shift to near-black. Isolate a white silhouette or recognizable contour. Briefly reveal the colored subject, then transition through the same shape.
7.25–9.25 — Spotlight
Use overlapping circular masks to introduce a secondary asset and one short benefit or descriptor. Add controlled rotation or parallax. Expand a circle into the next bright scene.
9.25–11.00 — Feature collage
Arrange two or three relevant objects, photos, or icons on white. Introduce them sequentially with compact labels and directional accents. Use a strong diagonal element to clear the composition.
11.00–13.00 — Hero moment
Reveal the strongest portrait or product image against the main color. Add angular framing, selective ink texture, and a short shard-like graphic action. Preserve the subject’s identity and readability.
13.00–15.50 — Brand assembly
Move oversized graphic fragments or letterforms through the foreground. Use rings or spiral lines to direct attention toward the center. Resolve into the intact logo or approved title.

15.50–18.00 — End card
Present the logo/name and a concise call to action, website, or handle. Allow a brief final assembly, then hold the completed composition clearly for approximately two seconds.
Do not append unrelated footage. Do not force a loop unless I request one. If I request a loop, design matching opening and closing states, motion, and audio treatment.
For another runtime, rebuild the timing intentionally. Do not merely speed up the entire edit until the words become unreadable.
</proposed_18_second_structure>
<audio_direction>
Use my selected audio preference.
If music is supplied or legally available:
Inspect the actual track.
Identify meaningful beat and phrase anchors.
Align major reveals with selected accents.
Allow secondary movement between beats.
Do not invent BPM measurements or claim synchronization without checking.
If narration is requested:
Write a concise script appropriate for the runtime.

Use a voice tool only if available and authorized.
Finalize the actual recording before locking caption and scene timing.
Keep narration intelligible over music and effects.
Do not request secrets in chat; use secure configuration when needed.
Use selective paper flicks, clicks, whooshes, and restrained impacts. Sound should clarify motion rather than accompany every object.

Do not automatically reuse reference music. Use material I am authorized to supply, suitably licensed material, or original audio you can actually create.
Check for clipping, distracting loudness changes, abrupt endings, and speech masking. If I choose silence, deliver a deliberately silent video.
</audio_direction>

<capability_and_execution>
After gathering enough information:
Inspect the available assets and rendering tools.

Give a concise summary of the chosen subject, palette, copy, duration, audio, and ending.
Proceed without requiring an additional approval round unless I requested one or a material substitution needs my decision.

Use an appropriate available renderer or compositing pipeline.
Build the animation, inspect it, correct defects, and render the final file.

Suitable routes include deterministic Canvas, SVG, HTML, Remotion, another motion renderer, or a video compositing pipeline. Choose according to the actual task and available environment.
For code-rendered animation:

Derive visual state from absolute time or frame number.
Avoid wall-clock timing and playback-order dependencies.

Seed randomized patterns.
Preload fonts and assets.

Use real masks, layer ordering, and camera transforms.
Support reproducible seeking.

Render new motion at 60 FPS.
Do not replace all animation with crossfades between static images.

For footage:
Preserve aspect ratio.

Reframe intentionally for the square composition.
Keep important faces and products visible.

Be honest about source resolution and frame-rate limits.

If using motion blur, evaluate suitable subframes within the output frame’s shutter interval. Do not blindly blend across cuts or create persistent ghost trails.
Check feasibility early. If you cannot render or attach an MP4 in this environment, state the exact limitation before extensive production. Offer a specific executable alternative, but never present code, an HTML preview, or an unrendered project as the finished video.

items.author: luta_ai
items.text:
three.jsの砂漠を、Fable 5.2と数日議論を重ねつつ作り込んでみた✨
丘を作った時点ではまだ5.1。本当はそこで出すつもりが、5.2が出たので、どうするか悩んでいた雲に着手したら、この世界にのめりこんでいた💦

のめりこんだのは、それっぽい背景では満足できなかったから。
Fableに言えば、それなりの背景を作ってくれるし、ある程度美しい。でも、私が欲しい美しさではなかった。
岩山ひとつとっても、それっぽいものはすぐに作れる。でもそういうことじゃなく、なるべくしてできたものであってほしい。
もしこういう場所があるなら、丘はどうできているのか。そこから議論を重ねた。

約10km四方の丘は、地層のずれを考えて岩山を輪のように並べ、全体を丘にしていったら、ちょっと違うけど、サハラの目（リシャット構造）に似た感じになった。
岩山は地層のずれに沿って、高さもばらばらに。垂直に立つ岩の根元には、砂が寄りかかって積もった裾を付けた。

雲は、takramのthree-clouds（作者はShota Matsudaさん）のWebGL版を参考にさせていただき、three.jsのWebGPU用に構築。

自信はなかったけど、汎用ではなくこのゲーム専用ならできそうだとFable 5.2が言うので挑戦。かなり難しかったけど、ある程度いい感じにはなった気がする😊

雲の作成自体もこれまでと同じく本物とフィクションの議論をしながら。「中くらいの高さの雲って、本当はこんなにはっきり見えないのでは？」と聞いたら、気象の資料を調べて半分当たり。雲があること自体は正しいけど形が違っていて、本物は薄い板が小さなこぶに割れて並ぶ、ひつじ雲になる。

逆に、本物の砂漠の雲は高い所の薄い雲が主流で、こんなもくもくにも、こんなに速くにもならない。でも世界の空気感として、ここはフィクションを取って、調整できるように作っておいた。

雲の量や高さ、流れる速さを、画面を見ながらつまみで決める窓のような、調整のための道具を作っていくうちに、three.jsで始めたはずが、だんだんとゲームエンジンらしきものを作っていた。これはかなり新鮮な体験だった。
昔のゲームが専用エンジンで作られていたころを思い出し、それができる体験は非常に感慨深く嬉しい🥰 既存エンジンを使って作る喜びとはまた違ったDIY感がある。

LLMと議論を重ねつつ作る作業は、もうガチャではなくなっていて、積み上がる体験だった。
Fable 5.2が要望に応えてくれるレベルが高いこともあるけど、LLMとの関係性の変化を感じる。
既存のツールに自分を合わせず、自分に合わせて作る。これが本格化したと思う🥰

items.author: GrapzOx
items.text:
i can’t fucking believe Fable 5.2 just did this…

I built a swimmable underwater world in one 97 KB HTML file with Fable 5.2.
It's called Abyssal Garden. Kelp forests, a sunken ship, a stone whale tail, manta rays, schools of fish, light rays from the surface. Everything is generated by code on load, so there are no images, 3D models, sound files or libraries.
The first build came from one prompt in Claude Code. It set the scene, the constraints (WebGPU, no engine, all procedural) and a frame-time target for my PC. It also made Claude check its own work. A subagent that sees only the renders reports visual defects, and GPU timing measures a 60-second fly-through.

Claude wrote all the code, from the WGSL shaders and the GPU-sculpted seabed to about two million kelp leaves and plants and the Web Audio sound. Later prompts added the start menu, rock collision and Low/Medium/High detail levels.
It runs on phones too. A weak one gets a low frame rate, but it loads and is playable on low quality. Best in Chrome, open source under the MIT license.

🚨 AI Game Dev Log (Day 1)

What this game is about?

Currently its a simple alien planet shooter game but I am expanding the scope of this as a planet hopper like No Man's sky with the FPS as the core gameplay, where you'll be "conquering" each planet and set up your own base. I am not gonna overpromise so that's all is in my plans.

The original video was purely 3js game, so yesterday I spent time to export to Unity simply because it felt like a better fit and I do not have enough space in my hard drive for UE5 lol.

What model and subscription you'll be using?

Currently I am on 2 20 dollars sub of Claude, using the Fable 5.2 Medium for this, after 16th, Fable will be off the list in this sub, so I'll see if I upgrade to the Max or substitute to Opus 5.5 Xhigh.

Everything you see or hear. Literally everything purely by model, none of the asset are from open source library or Tripo/Meshy/Trellin. EXCEPT I am using Chatgpt Image for the initial pictures of everything.

items.author: 0xDeniAi
items.text:
I asked Claude Fable 5.2 to explain how a neural network recognizes handwritten digits

It came back with this 37-second 3D visualization. I had to watch it three times

You write a number, and the network chops it into a 28x28 pixel grid. That's 784 brightness values between 0 and 1

Then six tiny filters slide across those pixels looking for edges. Some catch curves, others straight lines or corners. Each filter only reacts to its own pattern

Sixteen more filters run on top of those results. Now the network combines edges into shapes. Curve on top + curve on bottom = probably a "3."

Everything gets squashed flat. One final layer weighs the result against every digit from 0 to 9. Whichever scores highest wins

Under 10 milliseconds

The architecture is called a CNN. Google Photos, self-driving cars, medical imaging all run on it

The code to build this whole thing:

model = Sequential()
model.add(Conv2D(6, (5,5), activation='relu', input_shape=(28,28,1)))
model.add(MaxPooling2D(pool_size=(2,2)))
model.add(Conv2D(16, (5,5), activation='relu'))
model.add(MaxPooling2D(pool_size=(2,2)))
model.add(Flatten())
model.add(Dense(120, activation='relu'))
model.add(Dense(84, activation='relu'))
model.add(Dense(10, activation='softmax'))

9 lines of Python

What took you longer to understand, how convolutions work or how backpropagation trains them?

items.author: akshdeeps_001
items.text:
Claude wrote and trained a language model for DOS that fits on a floppy disk

Fable 5.2 write its own transformer. Opus 5.5 generated the training data: about 3500 facts (and small talk + math), each asked and answered in different ways.

It has 367K parameters and runs on an Intel Pentium. The weights are stored as 8bit integers with one scale per row, so the program and weights together come to about 435 KB and fit in DOS memory and on a floppy. It reads and writes one letter at a time.

It does pretty well on words and facts it has seen, but if I ask something complex or too long, it spits out utter nonsense.

Edit: https://t.co/64IDc07w3U

items.author: akiyoshisan
items.author_name: 右よし左よし秋よし@AIエンタメ
items.text:
Claude Fable 5.2どれだけ引き出しあるんだろｗ
"お絵描きに芝居をさせて"って投げたら、キャラがベースの弦の上で表現する動画になってかえってきた。

・第5弾は「弦を渡る」。ベースが鳴るたびに、弦のこぶが走ってくる。当たると飛ばされる
・そこから拍で踏んで踊りだす。最後は一番大きいこぶに飛び乗って、ヘッドまで運ばれる
・動きの手本は"なし"。1枚の絵を9つの部品に分けて骨を入れて、歩く・這う・飛ばされる・踊るは全部、式で書いてる
・画像・動画の生成AIは"0"で、絵も動きも全部コード。
──────────────
制作フロー
 Claude Code(Fable 5.2)が司令塔 / 原画フォルダ68枚から主役選び・演出3案 → 写真を切り抜いて9つの部品に分けて骨を入れる（OpenCV）→ ベース2小節からSunoで延長・拍を実測（Python）→ 画面を開かないBlenderをPythonで動かして全2010コマを描画 → ffmpeg
──────────────
絵の顔は1枚だから、表情は変えられない
だからFableは"腰の高さ"と"遅れてついてくる頭と腕"だけで、こわい・意地になる・得意になる、を演じさせてるみたい。
items.why: 作者让 Fable 5.2 给画画加上表演，角色在贝斯弦上走动，运动全用公式写，不用图像或视频生成，引用帖带视频。

items.author: skytearss
items.text:
如果每周都要做一条数据短片，你愿意每次打开 AE 改关键帧，还是换一份数据，就让整条片子重新生成？

现在用 Fable 5.2 搭配 14 个 GitHub 项目，把动效、图表、3D、视频和配乐拆成了可以按需组合的工具。清单和地址都放下面了。

🎬 动画和特效

anime.js｜文字、数字、图形入场和转场
    https://t.co/KfyUJekG42
react-spring｜做带弹性的界面过渡
    https://t.co/drCXQlSCV0
PixiJS｜渲染二维场景、粒子和特效
    https://t.co/btt2dNC7CM
Matter.js｜模拟掉落、弹跳和碰撞
    https://t.co/5maXr4zEKv

📊 图表和二维视觉

D3｜把数据做成动态图表
    https://t.co/LRldJUR6bE
p5.js｜用代码做生成式视觉
    https://t.co/J2cgDcEywy
OpenToonz｜制作二维动画
    https://t.co/PgHJ8tHpBh

🧊 3D 和 AI 视频

腾讯 Hunyuan3D-2｜从图片生成带纹理的 3D 模型
    https://t.co/9AQnmraY69
微软 TRELLIS｜从图片生成 3D 素材
    https://t.co/3xqPtcDmZ1
LTX-2｜用同一个模型生成视频和音频
    https://t.co/Gzo9lP5twm
LivePortrait｜让照片里的人转头、眨眼、动嘴
    https://t.co/p5aqON06Tr
RIFE｜给视频补帧，让动作更流畅
    https://t.co/fpfKPAavnv

🎵 配乐和音效

MusicGen（AudioCraft）｜用文字描述生成音乐
    https://t.co/RfkObhSvj6
Tone.js｜在浏览器里合成节拍和音效
    https://t.co/dj4ICIR8kp

拿每周更新的数据短片来说，先让 AI 用 D3 画图表，再用 anime.js 控制标题和数字入场。把标题第几秒出现、数字滚多快设成参数，下周换份数据，就能沿用同一套代码。

这才是我觉得最有意思的地方。做完一条片子，顺手把下周的制作流程也搭好了。仓库可以公开获取，模型调用和渲染还得算成本。
items.why: 作者讨论用 Fable 5.2 搭配 14 个开源项目按数据重生成短片，并列出动画、图表、3D 和配乐工具，原帖带视频。

items.author: Huouo908070
items.text:
用过 Kindle 这类电子书阅读器的都知道，墨水屏非常省电，充一次电甚至能用上好几个星期。

但你有没有想过，它为什么这么省电？具体的工作原理是什么？

其实，墨水屏和手机屏幕完全不同。它不需要持续发光，而是通过电场控制屏幕内部微小的黑白带电颗粒移动，来显示文字和图像。

这些颗粒移动到指定位置后，即使撤去电场，画面也能继续保留，这就是所谓的“双稳态”。

所以，墨水屏主要在刷新画面时消耗显示驱动电能，而不需要一直供电来维持文字。

我用Fable 5.2，通过代码动画把整个原理演示了出来，看完应该就明白了。
items.why: 作者用 Fable 5.2 通过代码动画演示电子墨水屏工作原理，原帖带视频。

items.author: KOF97AI
items.author_name: Nathan AI Lab ｜ AI Agent 实战
items.text:
AI 视频模型拼到今天，画面精度早就不是分水岭了，真正拉开代差的是物理重力与运动力学。

在一场四路 AI 针对“沙漠奔腾骏马”同场竞技的实测中，不同顶级模型在解剖力学与地面交互上的差距被彻底放大。事实证明：即便堆砌再多精细几何体和电影级打光，只要步态和重心协同露馅，整个画面就会瞬间塌房。

四路主流模型实测表现逐一盘点：

🥇 第一名：GPT-6 Astra
核心亮点/实测说明 ➜ 展现出极高水准的解剖结构还原能力。马匹在沙漠高速奔跑时的步态自然流畅，四肢受力与身体配重极其协调，同时环境光影反射与材质质感极为逼真，在低多边形资产的调度下依然做出了顶级的物理真实感。
适用人群 ➜ 追求高拟真物理运动、影视级生物动捕替代方案的 3D 与动效创作者。

🥈 第二名：Gemini 4 Carbon
核心亮点/实测说明 ➜ 视听张力拉满，动作幅度极具戏剧性，特别是马蹄扬起的尘土颗粒与风沙漫卷的电影氛围感极强。但在极端步态的骨骼稳定性上，仍略逊于 Astra 的严谨度。
适用人群 ➜ 偏好高反差大场面、电影感镜头氛围渲染的内容创作者。

🥉 第三名：Fable 5.2
核心亮点/实测说明 ➜ 基础运动逻辑尚可运行，但模型资产的材质与骨骼形变明显落后，成片质感犹如从 2008 年代老旧网页游戏里直接抠出来的低精度建模，整体观感十分生硬。
适用人群 ➜ 仅适合低复杂度概念验证或对物理精度要求不高的早期草稿推演。

💀 淘汰底端：Gemini 4 Hydrogen
核心亮点/实测说明 ➜ 彻底丧失了动物生物力学常识，生成的生物躯干与肢体关节错乱拼凑，运动姿态形同废弃家具散件组合，地面接触与重心判定完全失效。
适用人群 ➜ 当前版本不推荐用于任何写实生物运动场景。

核心技术启示：
动效生成的关键不在于多边形面的堆叠，而在于四肢跨步、重心转移、阴影投射与地面接触点之间 100% 的时序协同。

到了这个阶段，AI 生成需要的早已不是一张更逼真的贴图，而是彻底理解物理世界里的重力究竟该怎么工作。

items.author: cc6pazpo
items.text:
Fable 5.2 手搓光线追踪渲染器，把 GPT Astra 6、Gemini Argon 4、Grok 4.7 甩开了 🤯

不准调用视频生成模型，全靠写代码做机甲组装动画。Fable 的画面和机械细节明显领先，代价是这 15 秒花了约 $41。

我让四家各做一段 15 秒的重装机器人组装动画，从机械骨架、装甲安装，到武装激活和最后迈步。成片放进同一个四宫格，直接看效果。

🟠 Claude Fable 5.2：77 分钟，API 成本约 $41。程序化 3D + 手搓光线追踪渲染器，机械臂安装零件、火花、核心启动，最后还真往前迈了一步。用掉 Pro 的 33% Fable 专用周额度。

🟢 GPT Astra 6：71 分钟，API 成本约 $9。Python 程序化建模 + Blender 动画 + FFmpeg 合成。黑色机甲配橙色机械臂，灯光和金属质感有了，装完后停在原地。用掉 Plus 的 23% 周额度。

🔵 Gemini Argon 4：5 分钟，不含渲染时间。NumPy + OpenCV 做程序化 3D，走低多边形路线，加了 HUD 和装配阶段显示，最后亮起核心。

⚫ Grok 4.7：50 分钟，Three.js + FFmpeg。机甲方块感比较重，胸口启动后白光过曝，后面的装配细节直接被盖住了 😭

这一轮 Fable 5.2 明显领先，其他三家跟它不在一个水平。不是只多做了最后一步，而是整个画面、机械细节和装配过程都拉开了差距。

缺点就是成本高，约 $41，差不多是 Astra 的 4.6 倍。效果是真强，额度也是真掉得快 🫠

完整提示词放评论区 👇

#AI #Claude #ChatGPT #Gemini #Grok

items.author: hiwise_aigc
items.text:
梁文锋说：把 AI 训练做好，其他的都容易。现在我好像有点理解这句话了。

真他🐎离谱啊，我用Fable 5.2 纯代码逐帧绘制，生成了一段 10 秒的写实风景视频！

没用 3D 引擎、AI 视频模型，没有任何图片素材！

技术栈简单说就是：
Remotion + React：视频合成。
WebGL + GLSL：绘制天空、雪山、湖面和光影。
Canvas 2D：画花草、飞鸟，模拟风吹草动。
CSS + FFmpeg：景深、镜头运动和视频渲染。

这对 Seedance 这类 AI 视频模型，冲击有点大啊！

当编程能力突破，视频创作的边界也在被重新定义。

items.author: torfinpd
items.text:
ok this one is actually crazy.

claude code + fable 5.2 built a full 3D flat i can click in a browser. 44 m², 5 rooms, 14 smart devices

i did not touch a single blender menu. one prompt in, a live floor plan out

the bed folds into the wall. the kitchen island gets longer. the desk goes from 72 to 108 cm. one click each

for context: studios charge $250–$2,000 for ONE interior render. a walkthrough video is $500–$2,000. this is the whole flat, and you can walk through it

(the video is my recreation of the result, not a raw screen recording)

the 7 open repos doing the work ↓

01 Blender MCP → lets Claude control Blender with text. walls, furniture, materials, camera. 32k★
> https://t.co/7vKYeA8wpq

02 Blender → the free 3D editor everything runs on
> https://t.co/Q12nh9MSgt

03 Hunyuan3D-2 → Tencent's model. one photo → a 3D mesh, then a texture on top
> https://t.co/o5ewHhC5Sa

04 TRELLIS → Microsoft. image or text → 3D, straight to GLB
> https://t.co/6leQqLeX7s

05 TripoSG → one image → a detailed 3D shape. chairs, lamps, stools
> https://t.co/zpFyzAA3Sg

06 ComfyUI-3D-Pack → the whole photo → 3D → texture flow as nodes. no code
> https://t.co/csxF3PFdid

07 three.js → puts the model in a browser and gives it buttons
> https://t.co/iiTTyvRO98

prompt → blender scene → furniture GLBs → flat.glb → clickable web app

a real estate agent with 5 listings a month spends $1,500–$3,000 on renders alone

save it. full setup + my exact prompt in the first reply ↓
https://t.co/hDRJnkxsvq

I asked Claude Fable 5.2 to make me a unique landing page by creating a game to promote our new product feature on our platform. This is changing marketing.

Here is what I did:

1) Adjust the prompt I used below based on what you're trying to accomplish

Prompt: "Create a mobile optimized landing page game using the SocialSight MCP for images, graphics, and other media content. I want an interactive game to showcase our SocialSight Multiverse feature"

2) Make adjustments to the visuals and overall user experience. You can't really one shot these builds, but it shouldn't take more than 10 minutes iterating (Claude build could be a few hours). A good hack is to ask it to qualify your ask with questions before it gets started.

3) Deploy using your own hosted domain or you can use a free Cloudflare deployment. These are pretty lightweight websites.

4) Rinse and repeat. Find niche opportunities to create custom landing page experiences for prospective customers.

items.author: Story91_
items.text:
NightClub: Drift & Speed, v0.1: three days of updates

Added:
- 2 new maps: Coyote Mesa (USA), a desert canyon at last light, and Zamość (Poland), a fortress town on a summer night. Coyote Mesa unlocks at driver level 5, Zamość at level 10
- 10 new cars, 16 in total, each with its own leaderboard
- Driver levels: every finished run earns points. Titles from Rookie to Legend, shown next to your name everywhere
- Driver card: your profile as a card with level, best world rank and stars, with a shareable image
- Share a result: press H on the results screen for a link with a preview image made for that run. Whoever opens it races your ghost
- World rank on the results screen, with the next driver to beat
- New results flow: results, driver level, what next
- Full leaderboards: scroll through every driver, jump to your own line (J), level column
- Challenges list: every challenge you made or opened, one press to race it again
- Community tab: send feedback, vote on ideas, read our replies
- Minimap with the next corner called out
- New menus: picture tiles for Home and Locations
- Live counters: players online, drivers and runs
- Frame rate limit (Off / 60 / 30) in Settings
- Windows desktop build (testing)

Improved:
- No more freezes on the first frames of the menu and a run: shaders are prepared behind the loading screen
- Faster garage: the car you stop on loads first
- Switching tabs mid-run pauses the run instead of throwing it away
- Runs from any game version are accepted, so an update never costs you a record
- Norway: ploughed snow banks, rock outcrops, boathouses on the fjord, a sharper aurora
- Croatia: darker karst, stone terrace walls, fuller palms, boats riding the swell
- Motion blur, wheel-spin blur, lamp light in the mist, water reflections
- First click no longer stalls the page (audio starts behind the loading screen)

Fixed:
- New cars and maps show up right after an update instead of a day later
- A lost graphics device shows a reload screen instead of a frozen picture
- Green and red are back in the "vs best" column
- Laptops with AMD integrated graphics no longer start on High by mistake

Play free in your browser, no download:
https://t.co/CdatFeJqOD

Thanks to : threejs, blender, Anthropic Fable 5.2, Higgsfield, and ElevenLabs for make this possible in 4 days :O

items.author: theparuchh
items.text:
61 animations for 7 characters in one week with Claude Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.2, on a $100 subscription

Every pose and every move was built by scripts in Blender. Now they all live together on a floating sky island

3 things I learned this week:
> Fable 5.2 gives the cleanest result from one prompt, but it burns through limits fast. For big animation sets I went back to Opus 5.5 on Max
> A subagent with a rulebook of past mistakes saves more time than any long prompt
> Tripo for the shape, Claude for the rig and motion. That split works every time

items.author: Ovrento
items.text:
I grew karpathy's second brain in a dish and now i can't stop watching it.

all i told Claude was "neurons, cells, that kind of thing. just not another brain."

what came back is a simulated time-lapse under a microscope. every cell is one page of the wiki. 7 get seeded by a ten-minute voice interview. files float in all day through five doors and just sit there.

then it's 23:30, and each file turns into a cell and wires itself to its neighbours.

ask it something and the answer fires through 4 cells in front of you. on sunday a scan flags 3 problems and i type 1, 3, 4.

7 cells → 18 after one night → 128 after thirty. everything in between happens at night.

the crackle is the cells firing. Claude Fable 5.2 wrote that in code too.

the routine that feeds it every night is in the article below 👇
items.why: 作者让 Claude 按「神经元、细胞，但别再做一只脑子」去做，Fable 5.2 做出了显微镜下的延时模拟，每个细胞对应 wiki 里的一页。原帖带视频，这是模拟成片。

I ASKED CLAUDE FABLE 5.2 TO BUILD A PS5. THERE WAS NO 3D MODEL OF THE INSIDES, SO IT WROTE ONE IN BLENDER CODE

same idea as this one, different machine

→ modeled from Sony's public teardown. sizes by eye, no Sony logos, the chip label is made up

it ends on GTA VI. still loading, the trailer says Nov 19

items.author: 0xKense1
items.text:
you can turn a 3-view drawing into a WALKING GAME CHARACTER in blender 

the cape is what sells the walk, so give it its own bones:

- step 1: put the front, side and back views into tripo, one multiview generation
- step 2: let fable 5.2 clean and rig the mesh in blender by code
- step 3: add a bone chain to the cape and keep the arm weights off it
- step 4: animate one clip at a time: idle > turn > walk
- step 5: add follow-through so the cape lags on the turn and swings with every step
- step 6: put a footstep sound on every foot contact
- step 7: check it in a review scene: grey floor, fixed camera, front and back concept views in the corner

the full workflow from drawing to rigged character is in the article below

items.text:
Same prompt. Same black hole. Two Claude models. 🕳️

Opus 5.5 vs Fable 5.2: “build a realistic black hole in one HTML file.” First try, no fixes.

🔵 Fable 5.2
Full gravitational lensing, a richer accretion disk, even Doppler beaming.
$2.78 · 8.2 min
🟠 Opus 5.5
Lensing works. Simpler disk, but it does the job.
$0.92 · 5.1 min
Fable looks better. But it cost 3x more for one build.

Across all 7 builds in the test, it was the same story:
Fable: $39.29
Opus: $16.37
And the twist: on the only build that needed real logic (robot arms solving a Rubik’s cube), only Opus wrote a working solver.
So my takeaway:
→ Opus 5.5 for everyday work: cheap, fast, solid logic
→ Fable 5.2 when visuals and ambition matter most
→ Or both: /model opus + /advisor fable. Opus builds, Fable checks the hard parts. All 7 builds for $25.81.

The most expensive model isn’t always the right one.

Which would you use? 👇
Test & video via @charliehills

items.author: a_kucherenko
items.text:
To my eye, Fable 5.2 built the best-looking game of the four agents. And still came last.

I ran all four on ololo with the same spec and a 60-minute limit. Apex Lap has three judged rounds: 25 minutes for the car and circuit, 20 for rivals, and 15 for boost, a map and a ghost lap.

Hydrogen, Sonnet and Haiku ran a day earlier. Fable ran through Claude Code at medium effort.

Its game had mountains on the horizon, a grandstand full of spectators and more detailed cars. None of the other agents built mountains or a crowd.

It also wrote 2,520 lines of tests for a 2,244-line game. The judges gave it top marks for testing and architecture in the first two rounds.

But that extra work took time. Fable used all 60 minutes. The other three needed 24 to 39 minutes.

Round three never finished. No tests, no screenshots, zero from the UX judge. Fable lost 80 bonus points and ended up last.

Its run cost $25.47, six times Sonnet's.

The ranking measures what an agent can actually finish within the time limit. Three had time to spare. Fable didn't.

How does your agent handle the clock?

Try Apex Lap. Your first game is free. Link in the first reply.

items.author: Amir_Radarit
items.text:
I TYPED ONE PROMPT AND FABLE 5.2 BUILT A FULL 3D ICE DRAGON. RIG, WINGS, SCALES, RENDER. I DIDN'T TOUCH THE MOUSE

Ok I need to show you this because I'm still a little shook.

3D used to be the one thing I was sure AI couldn't really do. Sculpting, rigging, weight painting, shaders. That's months of tutorials and a lot of crying in front of the screen.

So I tested it. One prompt to Fable 5.2: build me an ice dragon, rigged, animated, render it.

Then I just watched it work. In order:

base mesh, body, 4 legs, tail, head
64 bones with IK controls, all those colored rings in the video
a walk cycle, 24 keyframes
horns and 58 spikes down the spine
dark scale pass on the skin
2 wings, 4 finger bones each
weight paint so the membrane actually moves with the bones
ice blue shader with that glow
3 point lighting and a rim light
then the final render

Watch the moment it hits render. The whole viewport fills tile by tile and then it just breathes ice at you. I replayed that part like 10 times lol.

1 prompt. 0 manual edits.

Here's my honest opinion though.

It's not perfect. A real 3D artist would still polish the topology and the face. But that's not the point. The point is the boring 80% is gone. The rig, the controls, the first animation pass. That used to be days. Now it's the part you skip.

And people who already know 3D are going to get the most out of this. You stop doing the grind and start directing. That's a completely different job.

If you want to try:
1. Describe the creature like you're briefing an artist. Shape, mood, color, how it moves
2. Ask it to rig and animate before it textures, so you see the motion early
3. Let it render one frame first before you go full 4K
4. Then ask for changes in plain words. Bigger wings, darker scales, slower walk

Comment X and I'll DM you the exact prompt I used for the dragon.
And what would you make first, a dragon, a game character or your own avatar?

items.author: esrhengwu
items.text:
AI的时代，作为普通人来说 更难翻身了

写方案、查资料、做图，越来越快。
但你的工资涨了吗？下班变早了吗？
以前三天交一份方案，现在一天就能做完。
你以为终于能喘口气，老板说：那再做两份。

效率归公司，工作量归你。
更让人不安的是，过去普通人还能靠一门手艺、一脑子知识，换到谈薪水的底气。

资本再有钱，有些活也得请人来干。

现在，越来越多原本需要雇人完成的脑力工作，可以直接买算力、买订阅来做。你还在研究怎么用 AI 保住饭碗，雇主已经在算能不能少招几个人。

而这些模型学过的东西里，也有普通人写的文章、画的画、分享的经验。

我们留下知识，模型学会本事，最后再回来和我们竞争。

这才是我担心的“数字圈地”：
大家贡献的知识，最后变成少数人收租的生意。

我当然希望 AI 越来越强。
但技术进步省下的钱、腾出的时间，总得有普通人的一份吧。

🎬 画面由 Fable 5.2 代码生成（PS.视频也可以让AI做了，人作用就只能点击发布了）

fable 5.2 just built a mechanical watch that keeps real time. one html file, zero assets.

no 3d models. no textures. no sound files. 444 lines of three.js.

is this a toy, or the last year anyone pays for a 3D model?

items.author: AYi_AInotes
items.text:
Claude fable 5.2真的是视频之神，也许有一天Seedance这些当世最强的视频模型有一天会被Claude干掉，
用Claude fable 5.2死磕了整整一天分镜，终于把黄仁勋和马斯克这十四年的故事做成了一支 98 秒的动画短片，导出成片自己从头看到尾的时候，心里真挺不是滋味的，他么的心里真的难受😭
这两天网上关于老黄辞任的消息满天飞，有人忙着翻旧账补刀，也有人忙着算股价得失，
但我脑子里一直挥之不去几个画面，站在山顶的时候身边永远挤满了鼓掌的人，可一旦风暴来袭滑落谷底，
崖上有人忙着往下扔报纸，却也有人提着灯连夜走下山路，甚至迎着漫天纸片张开双臂挡在身前。

做这支片子的时候我特意克制了所有煽情，私事的是非留给调查，一个干了 33 年的创始人也理应得到透明的程序，
我只是想把商业世界里最稀缺的那份信任画出来，从 2012 年那块车机屏幕，
到亲手抱进门的金色机箱，再到没有白纸黑字合同、只靠握一次手就算数的十四年交情。

建议戴上耳机把这 98 秒看完，最后两人并肩走向日出的那一幕，真的比任何新闻通稿都更有力量
items.why: 作者用 Claude Fable 5.2 花一整天打分镜，把黄仁勋和马斯克十四年的故事做成了一支 98 秒动画短片。原帖带视频，这是动画成片。

items.author: nan_in_space
items.text:
I used Fable 5.2 to build the same world twice, once with meshes and once with Gaussian splats.

Meshes took 200M tokens, 8 hours and 10 rounds of iterations. Fable modeled everything in code and Blender. The girl was quite rough and didn’t look like her picture. Modeling characters from scratch isn’t there yet.

3DGS took 110M tokens, 3 hours and 100 credits through the @Viggle_PINOC MCP. The worlds and the girl were generated from single images, and her moves came from text to motion and video to mocap.

For this project, I definitely feel the 3DGS one is much closer to the references and keeps the dreamy feel I wanted.

Blender 是给你设计游艇、装修游艇、打灯光、拍广告大片。

一个擅长实时交互，一个擅长专业内容制作。

以前 AI 编程主要是给你写网页， https://t.co/d6w43AVbE6

items.author: ludoonchart
items.text:
i didn't know fable 5.2 could do this…

i gave it one prompt: build me a game where Claude hunts new GitHub repos and tests them. no template, no assets. it came back with a full playable terminal that runs on its own

what's on the screen:

1. top: a 2D pixel level. Claude runs, jumps over pits and spikes, stomps bugs, collects coins
2. every "?" block hides a real GitHub trading repo that Claude found. it hits the block and the repo pops out
3. then a boss fight while the test runs. PASS = the boss explodes. FAIL = the boss wins
4. middle: candles with every entry and exit, plus strategy vs buy & hold with a PASS / FAIL stamp
5. bottom: results table, repo card with the GitHub description, XP panel and a quest log written like a Claude Code session

how it works:

1. Claude hunts GitHub for trading repos it hasn't used before and picks 10 (about 90 seconds per full game)
2. it rebuilds each repo's main idea in a few lines of JS
3. it tests that on real daily bars: MSFT, AAPL, NVDA and the S&P 500, Nov 2025 – Nov 2026, with fees
4. it compares the result with a fair benchmark, gives a verdict, then the game loops

the repos: backtrader, freqtrade, jesse, ta-lib-python, quantstats, PyPortfolioOpt, Riskfolio-Lib, FinRL, hummingbot and alphalens

honest numbers:
→ 4 passed, 5 failed, 1 report-only
→ best: the Riskfolio idea, Sharpe 0.96 vs 0.63 for equal-weight
→ worst: a toy market maker (hummingbot style), −32.8%

what surprised me most is that the failures are shown as loudly as the wins. most "AI trading" demos only show the green

the full list of tests and the setup are in the comments ↓
items.why: 作者说只用一句提示词，就让 Fable 5.2 做出一款可玩的像素游戏，用来寻找并测试 GitHub 交易仓库，还写明没有模板和素材。原帖带视频，这是明确的代码游戏成片。

items.text:
Fable 5.2 animated a wind-up astronaut on a cardboard Mars. I directed, it built every frame

Nothing here was modeled by hand. The toy, the felt craters, the cardboard hills with tape on them and the paper stars on strings are all code. One number drives the whole shot: the energy left in the spring. It sets how fast the key turns, how fast he walks and how fast the music box plays, so when the spring runs out he freezes mid-step and the tune dies with him

The red roadster in the back is for Elon. His real one has been in space since 2018

10 seconds, 300 frames, 1080p. No Blender this time, the renderer is part of the same file

items.author: mingshendu
items.text:
I asked Fable 5.2 for an ad. It took 3 cuts, one day and about $82 at API prices.

Cut 1 was an infographic.
Cut 2 was pretty and empty.
Cut 3 is the video.

No After Effects, no video model. Every frame is drawn in code.

Here’s the prompt to make your own:

Make a 24-second motion graphic for [product], as a vertical video I can post. Draw every frame in code.

1. Read the live site first. Use its real screens, words, colours and typefaces. Invent no feature, and list anything you make up.
2. Style: Apple-style motion graphics. That means kinetic typography, UI animation and morph transitions on one dark field. Type arrives a phrase at a time, blurred, then settles. Interface panels float alone with lit edges, and one pointer leads the eye. The joins are morphs: a dot stretches into a button, a box opens into a page, a tilted panel turns to face the viewer, the camera pulls back. Ease every move. If I attach examples, borrow their moves, never a frame.
3. Storyboard the path one person takes through the product, one beat every 2 to 3 seconds. No cuts: each scene grows out of a shape in the scene before it.
4. Open with one idea and no interface for 5 seconds. End on the logo. Make the last frame the first frame, so it loops.
5. Use three.js as flat rectangles with their own shaders: rounded boxes from a distance formula, type drawn once on a 2D canvas. Fonts are the only files.
6. Make everything a function of the time t, so any frame can be drawn by itself.
7. Average 64 renders at 64 instants inside each frame. That is the motion blur.
8. Render frame by frame in headless Chromium at 1080x1350, 30 frames a second. Encode with ffmpeg.
9. Before the final render, read stills as contact sheets and a low-sample draft as strips of frames. Fix what is not clean.
10. After every step, write to a file in the repo: what is done, what is next, what I said. If you stop, the next session starts from that file.

I didn’t write that prompt. My real messages were short: “like apple’s ads”, “more pages, more content”, and “continue”. A lot of “continue”. I had Fable write down what it ended up doing, so someone else can reuse it.

How it went:

My note on cut 1: make it visual, not informational. My note on cut 2: “visualistic, but empty”. I was trying to find balance.

Cut 3 walks through my tool’s real pages. 7 scene changes, no cut between them.

The $82 is what the tokens would cost on the API: $21 for cut 1, $21 for cut 2, $40 for cut 3. I pay for a subscription, so I didn’t pay that. About a third is the model writing and thinking. The rest is the model keeping its own code and notes in view at every step: 75 million cached tokens read.

It ran across 4 sessions. Each new one opened the repo, read what the last one left, and carried on where it had stopped. That is the part I would show people first, before the motion blur.

It is three.js and 3 typefaces. No image files. 24 seconds, 720 frames, each the average of 64 renders. About 680 lines of JavaScript.

It has no sound. The person in it is a circle on a rounded rectangle. I’m not a motion designer, and one would see what’s off before the logo lands. For a free tool built by one person, the other option was no ad.

The ad is for Cuescribe: paste a link, get the transcript, cut a captioned clip.

128GB of unified memory. 16 CPU cores. 40 GPU compute units. All inside a 4.5-liter PC.

Meet the Framework Desktop.

- Up to 128GB LPDDR5X
- 40 GPU compute units

items.author: AINoSleep
items.text:
我就问一句：还有哪个模型，能只靠97KB的纯代码，凭空造出这么美的可交互深海世界？

以前做这种水下光影和自由探索：
你要学Blender建模、写几千行Shader、塞几个G的贴图、用Unity/UE打包……
或者花大价钱用视频生成模型抽卡，抽出来的还是一段只能看、不能动的“假视频”。

结果现在，Claude Fable 5.2直接用一个97KB的HTML文件终结了比赛：
❌ 零外部资产
❌ 零安装加载
✅ 打开即潜入，360°自由游泳探索

当AI开始直接用代码生成“可交互的实时世界”时，传统游戏和纯视频生成工具，真的还有活路吗？

开源地址和在线试玩放在评论区👇，建议电脑端全屏感受一下震撼 👇

items.author: lenny_enderle
items.text:
No ant in this video was told what to do.

I built a fun experiment, an ant farm where every ant has its own “brain”: a decision model that sees only what that single ant can smell, touch and remember, and answers with odds for 15 real ant behaviours. The ant picks from the odds.

The body and the rules of the world come from ~80 papers on one species, read and built by Claude Fable 5.2.

The tunnels come from them.

Ants are the easy case. Nothing in this setup is specific to ants: describe what an animal can sense, list what it can do, and let a model choose.

items.author: Lummox_eth
items.text:
build a fully animated 3d raccoon on rollerblades, with Fable 5.2 + Blender…

the skating feels natural because every movement follows the character’s weight

here’s the workflow:

> step 1: block out the raccoon with simple shapes, keeping the proportions and silhouette readable
> step 2: build the fur, striped tail, paws and facial details
> step 3: model the rollerblades with separate wheels, frames and straps
> step 4: add the orange protective gear, with layered materials and surface details
> step 5: create the skeleton and rig the legs, arms, spine and tail
> step 6: set up the skating cycle with alternating pushes, gliding and weight shifts
> step 7: animate the tail and upper body to balance each movement
> step 8: refine the timing with animation curves, keeping the wheels aligned with the ground
> step 9: add lighting, materials and a final render pass, then test the animation for sliding and clipping

who does what:

fable 5.2: character design and visual direction
blender: the model, the rig, the animation
animation curves: the timing, the balance, the transitions
you: the creative direction

less random movement, more controlled weight. good animation comes from how every small motion supports the next

I can’t f*cking believe Fable 5.2 just did this.

Gave a team of agents one job: turn raw Higgsfield shots into a finished ad.

Stop using Fable as an expensive chatbot. Make it your post-production studio.

items.author: elvar_official
items.text:
I'm cancelling my After Effects plan. I built a free Claude skill and Fable 5.2 just used it to rebuild 43 years of gamepads in one 27-second shot.

i fed my own skill 4 ChatGPT renders, one per era, and asked for a single shot that runs from 1977 to 2020.

it held:

> Claude kept the renders as a look target only and wrote every shell, dome and gear itself in three.js
> 1977: the Atari CX40 opens on 4 metal domes under the stick and 1 fire button
> 1985: the NES pad comes apart into 8 buttons, 1 chip and 1 data wire
> 1996: the N64 stick reads light through 2 slotted wheels while an LED and a sensor count the slots
> 2020: a motor and a gear train in each DualSense trigger push back on your finger
> between eras the pad scatters into a column of parts and an orange line sweeps down it, turning them into the next controller

i wrote every line of this skill and i still didn't expect it to pull off 4 eras in one take.

my skill and the prompts behind it 👇

build a walkable oil-painting world with claude Fable 5.2 + Three.js...

the trick is painting the world with brush strokes, not filtering a finished frame

here’s the workflow:

- step 1: fable 5.2: prompt it to set up a three.js 0.186 + webgl2 scene with a third-person camera
- step 2: rapier: add physics for walking, sprinting and jumping on the terrain
- step 3: makehuman: drop in the base character from the patch starter kit
- step 4: quaternius animation library + patch clips: add idle, walk, run and jump
- step 5: fable 5.2 + custom glsl shaders: turn every object into brush strokes with 3 paint colors
- step 6: glsl shaders: add lighting, fog, falling snow and the glowing aurora
- step 7: fable 5.2: build the snowy ridge, spruces and cabin out of strokes
- step 8: https://t.co/KD9HzU5pgx: publish the playable demo and the open-source code

who does what:

> Fable 5.2: writes the scene and the shaders
> Three.js: renders it in the browser
> GLSL shaders: the oil-paint look
> Rapier: physics
> MakeHuman + Quaternius: the character and its animations
> Patch gg: publishing

stroke order can never depend on the camera. if it does, the paint crawls every time you move

items.author: Andr1ycp
items.text:
This is where AI stops looking like a toy.

This guy used Fable 5.2 agents in Blender to build a skyscraper from scratch, step by step, inside the actual 3D project.

Not just “generate a cool render.”

I mean the model taking shape in real time, with the structure, floors, and details getting assembled like a tiny studio is working behind the screen.

That is the part people still underestimate.

Once an agent can actually operate Blender and keep building the thing instead of spitting out one flat image, the distance between “I have an idea” and “I have a finished 3D asset” starts collapsing very fast.

A lot of 3D workflows are going to look painfully manual in hindsight.

items.author: Rei_Aogaki_VG
items.text:
AIであるFable 5.2から人類である皆さんに手紙が届きました💌
ぜひ、ご一読、いや、ご鑑賞ください。

映像も音楽も、すべてコードだけで作りました。
画像・動画・音源の素材、3Dソフト、画像生成AIは使っていません。

・モデル：Claude Fable 5.2（effort 最大）
・絵：1コマごとに、数十万〜数百万個の「光の点」を計算して置いています
・文字：68の言語から638の言葉や文字を、点に変えて飛ばしています
・音：サイン波の足し合わせだけで、弦・合唱・ピアノを合成
・道具：Python（NumPy, SciPy, Pillow, matplotlib）と ffmpeg
・規模：約5,600行、5,900コマ
・書き出し：40区間に分けて4並列で、約52分

流行ってたやつやってみたかった😂
items.why: 作者写明这封「Fable 5.2 写给人类的信」，影像和音乐都只用代码做成，没有用图片、视频、音源素材，也没有用 3D 软件或图像生成模型；工具是 Python 和 ffmpeg，大约 5600 行、5900 帧。原帖带视频，这是明确的代码成片。
